jobs.description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

In 1965, the University of California, Irvine was founded with a mission to catalyze the community and enhance lives through rigorous academics, cutting-edge research, and dedicated public service. A top public university, UCI has become internationally recognized for improving lives through research and discovery, fostering excellence in scholarship and teaching, and engaging and enriching the community. Today, UCI continues to inspire change and pioneer new ideas with the support of its generous partners, alumni and friends.

Through the combined efforts of the University Advancement & Alumni relations team, the university is able to share its amazing achievements, build lasting relationships and generate support for important campus programs and initiatives. University Advancement seeks to strengthen contributions in research, education, and service; accelerate the university's place among globally preeminent research universities; and bring together passions, skills, and creativity to further improve people's lives.

Your Role on the Team

The Director of Development is a fundraising professional who works collaboratively with the Senior Executive Director of Development (SrEDOD) for Cancer and UCI Health System Programs and University Advancement (UA) colleagues to lead specific development programs for UCI Health within the Chao Family Comprehensive Cancer Center and other departments and divisions that are cancer adjacent, securing significant philanthropic investments to support these areas. The primary activity of the Director of Development is externally focused to secure private philanthropic support and the Director of Development’s effectiveness will be evaluated on the ability to achieve financial goals and meet metrics. The Director of Development reports to the Senior Executive Director of Development, Health Advancement. The Director of Development is expected to be a highly collaborative colleague with other development officers on the Health Advancement team and across the campus.

Required

What It Takes to be Successful

Advanced knowledge of all aspects of fundraising, donor relations, and public relations concepts, principles, procedures, and techniques.
Advanced working knowledge of all aspects of the location, including current issues of concern for both the campus and / or throughout higher education / healthcare generally. Advanced working knowledge of the location, its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure.
Advanced knowledge of applicable laws, rules, regulations, policies, etc.
Advanced written, oral and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships throughout the organization and with outside constituencies. Ability to make persuasive and compelling presentations of goals and objectives for a location in order to secure gifts.
Advanced organizational, analytical and critical thinking skills, including skill in creative and effective decision-making and problem identification / avoidance / resolution, and strong project management skills.
Very strong skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Ability to prepare complex and detailed proposals and related materials.
Highly organized and able to handle multiple projects.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Salesforce or a comparable donor/prospect database system.
Demonstrable experience in stewardship plans leading to additional investments.
Clarity of focus while juggling complex projects and/or deadlines. Ability to meet demanding work schedule expectations.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Five years' successful professional development and/or fundraising-related experience, preferably in higher education, OR, any equivalent combinations of education and/or experience from which comparable knowledge, skill and abilities have been achieved.

Special Conditions

May work long hours to meet fundraising commitments
Local, regional, and national travel

Total Rewards

In addition to the salary range listed below, we offer a wealth of benefits to make working at UCI even more rewarding. These benefits may include medical insurance, sick and vacation time, retirement savings plans, and access to a number of discounts and perks. Please utilize the links listed here to learn more about our compensation practices and benefits.

The expected pay range for this recruitment is $111,300- $130,000 (Annual).

jobs.title: Executive Director, Maintenance Operations
jobs.description:
When you join the growing BILH team, you're not just taking a job, you’re making a difference in people’s lives.

The Executive Director of Maintenance Operations provides enterprise-wide leadership, strategic direction, operational oversight, and regulatory compliance for maintenance operations across multiple regional hospitals in the Beth Israel Lahey Health (BILH) system. This role is responsible for driving standardization, reliability, safety, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across multiple hospitals and community sites while ensuring regulatory readiness and effective stewardship of physical assets and infrastructure. This role ensures that each facility operates at optimal efficiency, safety, and reliability while maintaining compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations. They will lead a multidisciplinary team of directors, managers, and technicians and collaborate with hospital leadership, construction, engineering, and clinical departments to support continuous, system-wide process improvement in facilities maintenance. The role will operate within a matrixed organizational structure, with both direct and indirect reporting relationships across BILH. Responsible for oversight of maintenance operations supporting multiple acute care hospitals, ambulatory facilities, and community sites across the BILH system.

Job Description

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
including but not limited to:

Strategic Leadership & Planning

Develop and implement a system-wide maintenance strategy aligned with organizational goals.
Identify and assist in managing capital and operational budgets for maintenance operations across all BILH hospitals.
Establish performance benchmarks, KPIs, and reporting metrics to monitor and optimize maintenance outcomes.
Collaborate with executive leadership on long-term facility planning, sustainability, and infrastructure modernization.
Develop and implement an asset management strategy
Identify continuous improvement initiatives
Evaluate and standardize workforce planning
Establish and monitor system-wide maintenance performance standards, productivity metrics, and service level expectations.
Ensure consistency in maintenance operations, staffing models, and service delivery practices across facilities.

Operational Oversight

Monitor the maintenance operations for assigned hospitals within the BILH system, ensuring 24/7 readiness of critical systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, life safety, medical gas, etc.).
Lead standardization of maintenance procedures, preventive maintenance programs, and work order systems across the system.
Partner with Director of Vendor Services to manage vendors, contract negotiations, and procurement related to maintenance services and equipment.
Lead emergency preparedness efforts related to infrastructure failure, disaster recovery, and utility interruption.
Lead the implementation and successful adoption of system-wide maintenance standards and initiatives across BILH

Regulatory Compliance & Safety

Monitor and audit facility conditions to ensure patient, staff, and visitor safety.
Work closely with hospital engineering and environmental services teams to support accreditation and inspection readiness.
Ensure ongoing survey readiness and compliance with all applicable regulatory and accreditation requirements including TJC, CMS, OSHA, NFPA, EPA, state, and local regulations.
Lead corrective action planning and compliance remediation efforts resulting from regulatory inspections and audits.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team including directors, facility managers, engineers, and skilled trades staff.
Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer service.
Implement training programs and succession planning to ensure skilled workforce continuity.
Lead organizational change management efforts associated with implementation of enterprise maintenance programs, standards, and technologies.
Provide leadership and direction to site-based directors and managers while promoting consistency in operational performance across the system.
Develop leadership talent and succession plans to build organizational capability and workforce sustainability

Education

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, or related field. Relevant experience may be substituted for the educational requirement.

Licensure, Certification & Registration

Certified Healthcare Facility Manager (CHFM) preferred.

Experience

Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare facilities management or maintenance operations.
Experience overseeing multi-site or system-level operations in a hospital or large healthcare setting is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience managing large teams, complex infrastructure, and multimillion-dollar budgets.

Skills, Knowledge & Abilities

Strong knowledge of building systems, life safety codes, and hospital maintenance best practices.
Exceptional leadership, organizational, and communication skills.
Ability to lead cross-functional teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare environment.
Proficiency in CMMS, project management tools, and data-driven decision-making.
Demonstrated financial management skills with experience overseeing capital and operating budgets.
Ability to analyze operational and financial data and translate insights into strategic decisions
Ability to travel regularly between facilities across the hospital system is required.

Pay Range

$150,000.00 USD - $225,000.00 USD

Actual compensation is determined based on several factors, that may include seniority, education, training, relevant experience, relevant certifications, geography of work location, job responsibilities, or other applicable factors permissible by law.

jobs.description:
Director of Operations — Sterling Construction and Roofing

Kingfisher Recruiting has been hired to find a Director of Operations for Sterling Construction in Livonia, MI. This is an established growing construction company that is looking to hire its first Director of Operations. This is a new role that is foundational to grow the company

About Sterling Construction and Roofing

Sterling Construction and Roofing is a Metro Detroit construction and roofing company serving residential, commercial, multi-family, HOA/condominium, and public-sector clients. The role is based in Livonia, Michigan, with a target candidate commute of roughly 20 minutes. The company is seeking a senior operations leader who can translate the Owner/CEO’s vision, growth priorities, and financial expectations into disciplined daily execution.

Position Summary

The Director of Operations is the senior leader responsible for running the company’s day-to-day operating system. This person will free the Owner/CEO from routine operational management by building clear accountability, repeatable processes, reliable reporting, and a leadership cadence that keeps production, project delivery, customer experience, quality, safety, and profitability on track.

This is an executive operating role for someone with General Contractor construction operations experience — not an office manager, controller, bookkeeper, generic field-services operator, or transactional administrative position. The right person will be comfortable leading field and office leaders, solving cross-functional bottlenecks, making timely decisions, and creating an owner-light organization that runs with discipline.

Reporting Relationship

The Director of Operations reports directly to the Owner/CEO and provides leadership, direction, and accountability to production managers, project managers, field or crew leaders, office or administrative leaders as assigned, and other department leaders designated by the Owner.

Key Responsibilities

Operating Cadence and Leadership Accountability

Lead a disciplined weekly leadership rhythm, including L10-style meetings or a similar operating cadence.
Maintain a scorecard of key operational, financial, customer, people, safety, and systems metrics.
Set weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual priorities with clear owners and follow-through.
Resolve routine cross-departmental issues without unnecessary Owner intervention.
Conduct recurring one-on-ones, performance reviews, and coaching sessions with direct reports.
Provide the Owner/CEO concise executive reporting on results, forecast changes, material risks, decisions needed, and corrective actions.

Production and Project Delivery

Own the project delivery operating system from production-ready handoff through closeout.
Maintain a realistic production plan aligned with capacity, crews, subcontractors, materials, permits, inspections, equipment, customer commitments, and sequencing.
Ensure every project has an accountable owner, current schedule, documented milestones, and timely constraint identification.
Direct project, production, and field leaders to protect schedule, scope, quality, safety, communication, and margin.
Establish recovery processes for delayed, over-budget, customer-sensitive, quality-sensitive, or otherwise at-risk jobs.
Maintain a reliable closeout process covering customer communication, quality verification, documentation, billing readiness, warranty prevention, and lessons learned.

Financial and Operating Performance

Monitor operational drivers of profitable execution, including revenue produced, backlog health, production capacity, gross profit, job-cost variance, labor/material efficiency, rework, warranty exposure, and operating forecast.
Ensure leaders submit accurate production, job-cost, change-order, completion, and closeout information for reliable reporting.
Identify margin leakage, waste, process failures, and recurring cost issues, then lead corrective action.
Coordinate with accounting/controller functions on billing milestones, cash forecasting, collections risk, WIP reporting, and financial planning inputs.

Sales-to-Production Alignment

Establish and enforce a production-ready handoff checklist between sales and production.
Confirm scope, pricing, documentation, customer expectations, financing/payment requirements, permits, material selections, special conditions, and change-order status before jobs enter the production schedule.
Maintain capacity, backlog, and sales-commitment discussions with sales leadership.
Identify sales commitments that create avoidable capacity, margin, quality, customer, or scheduling risk.
Create feedback loops from production and customer outcomes back into sales training, estimating assumptions, and process improvement.

Customer Experience and Quality

Ensure customers receive timely, accurate, professional communication during production and closeout.
Lead resolution of escalated operational customer issues within delegated authority.
Establish response and escalation expectations for customer concerns, warranty callbacks, scope questions, schedule changes, and closeout issues.
Monitor customer satisfaction, reviews, complaints, repeat issues, warranty callbacks, and quality trends.
Require documented corrective action for recurring customer or quality failures.

Team Leadership and Talent Development

Build a leadership team capable of performing without daily Owner intervention.
Maintain clear role scorecards, responsibilities, authority boundaries, and performance expectations.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, training, coaching, succession planning, performance management, and termination recommendations.
Address poor performance, conflict, conduct concerns, and leadership gaps directly and promptly.
Develop managers so routine decisions are made at the appropriate level rather than pushed upward.

Systems, Data, and Continuous Improvement

Standardize workflows, SOPs, checklists, handoffs, dashboards, meetings, and escalation procedures.
Require accurate use of CRM, project-management, and reporting systems.
Eliminate duplicate effort, unnecessary manual work, information gaps, and recurring bottlenecks.
Prioritize automation and system improvements that improve visibility, accountability, speed, quality, and customer experience.
Ensure process changes are documented, trained, adopted, measured, and improved.

Compliance, Safety, and Risk Management

Ensure operational leaders maintain required safety, licensing, insurance, permit, labor, contract, and project-documentation practices.
Maintain a visible safety and quality culture with timely reporting, investigation, corrective action, and coaching.
Escalate serious safety incidents, fraud/theft, property damage, threatened litigation, regulatory matters, warranty exposure, insurance claims, or material brand risk promptly to the Owner.
Ensure responsible leaders track permits, inspections, contractual requirements, prevailing-wage/government-project requirements, and other compliance obligations.

First 90-Day Expectations

Days 1–30

Complete an initial operating assessment.
Establish KPI baseline and dashboard.
Map the sales-to-production-to-closeout workflow.
Identify recurring Owner operational interventions.
Clarify decision rights and escalation paths.
Begin the weekly leadership cadence.

Days 31–60

Implement a production-ready handoff checklist.
Publish leader scorecards.
Establish schedule and capacity reviews.
Assign accountable owners for recurring bottlenecks.
Present a written operating-improvement plan with priorities, owners, dates, and expected outcomes.

Days 61–90

Demonstrate an owner-light operating rhythm.
Provide reliable weekly executive reporting.
Show measurable improvement or a documented recovery plan for critical bottlenecks.
Lead the first formal leader scorecard reviews.
Present the next 90-day operating priorities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Senior operations leader with General Contractor construction operations experience.
Proven ability to lead production, project delivery, field teams, project managers, subcontractors, and cross-functional operating cadence.
Strong understanding of subcontractors, invoicing/billing readiness, permits/inspections, scheduling, capacity planning, vendor/material coordination, job-cost control, margin protection, quality, safety, customer escalation, and closeout.
Comfortable building dashboards, scorecards, SOPs, leadership meeting rhythms, and accountability systems.
Able to work closely with an Owner/CEO while independently owning routine operational decisions.
Direct, accountable, values-driven leader who can address hard issues respectfully and promptly.

Key Performance Areas

Revenue produced versus plan and backlog health.
Gross profit, job-cost variance, and margin leakage correction.
Job cycle time, production-ready backlog, schedule stability, and on-time completion.
Billing readiness, WIP coordination, and collections-risk reduction from operational delays.
Customer satisfaction, complaint resolution, review trends, warranty callbacks, and quality performance.
Safety incidents, near misses, training completion, permit/licensing/compliance exceptions, and corrective-action closure.
Leadership scorecard attainment, retention, manager development, and performance review completion.
CRM/project-system data accuracy, SOP adoption, dashboard quality, and continuous improvement.

Responsible for oversight of maintenance operations supporting multiple acute care hospitals, ambulatory facilities, and community sites across the BILH system.

Identify continuous improvement initiatives

Director of Operations — Sterling Construction and Roofing

Kingfisher Recruiting has been hired to find a Director of Operations for Sterling Construction in Livonia, MI. This is an established growing construction company that is looking to hire its first Director of Operations. This is a new role that is foundational to grow the company

About Sterling Construction and Roofing

Sterling Construction and Roofing is a Metro Detroit construction and roofing company serving residential, commercial, multi-family, HOA/condominium, and public-sector clients. The role is based in Livonia, Michigan, with a target candidate commute of roughly 20 minutes. The company is seeking a senior operations leader who can translate the Owner/CEO’s vision, growth priorities, and financial expectations into disciplined daily execution.

Position Summary

The Director of Operations is the senior leader responsible for running the company’s day-to-day operating system. This person will free the Owner/CEO from routine operational management by building clear accountability, repeatable processes, reliable reporting, and a leadership cadence that keeps production, project delivery, customer experience, quality, safety, and profitability on track.

This is an executive operating role for someone with General Contractor construction operations experience — not an office manager, controller, bookkeeper, generic field-services operator, or transactional administrative position. The right person will be comfortable leading field and office leaders, solving cross-functional bottlenecks, making timely decisions, and creating an owner-light organization that runs with discipline.

Reporting Relationship

The Director of Operations reports directly to the Owner/CEO and provides leadership, direction, and accountability to production managers, project managers, field or crew leaders, office or administrative leaders as assigned, and other department leaders designated by the Owner.

Key Responsibilities

Operating Cadence and Leadership Accountability

Lead a disciplined weekly leadership rhythm, including L10-style meetings or a similar operating cadence.
Maintain a scorecard of key operational, financial, customer, people, safety, and systems metrics.
Set weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual priorities with clear owners and follow-through.
Resolve routine cross-departmental issues without unnecessary Owner intervention.
Conduct recurring one-on-ones, performance reviews, and coaching sessions with direct reports.
Provide the Owner/CEO concise executive reporting on results, forecast changes, material risks, decisions needed, and corrective actions.

Production and Project Delivery

Own the project delivery operating system from production-ready handoff through closeout.
Maintain a realistic production plan aligned with capacity, crews, subcontractors, materials, permits, inspections, equipment, customer commitments, and sequencing.
Ensure every project has an accountable owner, current schedule, documented milestones, and timely constraint identification.
Direct project, production, and field leaders to protect schedule, scope, quality, safety, communication, and margin.
Establish recovery processes for delayed, over-budget, customer-sensitive, quality-sensitive, or otherwise at-risk jobs.
Maintain a reliable closeout process covering customer communication, quality verification, documentation, billing readiness, warranty prevention, and lessons learned.

Financial and Operating Performance

Monitor operational drivers of profitable execution, including revenue produced, backlog health, production capacity, gross profit, job-cost variance, labor/material efficiency, rework, warranty exposure, and operating forecast.
Ensure leaders submit accurate production, job-cost, change-order, completion, and closeout information for reliable reporting.
Identify margin leakage, waste, process failures, and recurring cost issues, then lead corrective action.
Coordinate with accounting/controller functions on billing milestones, cash forecasting, collections risk, WIP reporting, and financial planning inputs.

Sales-to-Production Alignment

Establish and enforce a production-ready handoff checklist between sales and production.
Confirm scope, pricing, documentation, customer expectations, financing/payment requirements, permits, material selections, special conditions, and change-order status before jobs enter the production schedule.
Maintain capacity, backlog, and sales-commitment discussions with sales leadership.
Identify sales commitments that create avoidable capacity, margin, quality, customer, or scheduling risk.
Create feedback loops from production and customer outcomes back into sales training, estimating assumptions, and process improvement.

Customer Experience and Quality

Ensure customers receive timely, accurate, professional communication during production and closeout.
Lead resolution of escalated operational customer issues within delegated authority.
Establish response and escalation expectations for customer concerns, warranty callbacks, scope questions, schedule changes, and closeout issues.
Monitor customer satisfaction, reviews, complaints, repeat issues, warranty callbacks, and quality trends.
Require documented corrective action for recurring customer or quality failures.

Team Leadership and Talent Development

Build a leadership team capable of performing without daily Owner intervention.
Maintain clear role scorecards, responsibilities, authority boundaries, and performance expectations.
Participate in hiring, onboarding, training, coaching, succession planning, performance management, and termination recommendations.
Address poor performance, conflict, conduct concerns, and leadership gaps directly and promptly.
Develop managers so routine decisions are made at the appropriate level rather than pushed upward.

Systems, Data, and Continuous Improvement

Standardize workflows, SOPs, checklists, handoffs, dashboards, meetings, and escalation procedures.
Require accurate use of CRM, project-management, and reporting systems.
Eliminate duplicate effort, unnecessary manual work, information gaps, and recurring bottlenecks.
Prioritize automation and system improvements that improve visibility, accountability, speed, quality, and customer experience.
Ensure process changes are documented, trained, adopted, measured, and improved.

Compliance, Safety, and Risk Management

Ensure operational leaders maintain required safety, licensing, insurance, permit, labor, contract, and project-documentation practices.
Maintain a visible safety and quality culture with timely reporting, investigation, corrective action, and coaching.
Escalate serious safety incidents, fraud/theft, property damage, threatened litigation, regulatory matters, warranty exposure, insurance claims, or material brand risk promptly to the Owner.
Ensure responsible leaders track permits, inspections, contractual requirements, prevailing-wage/government-project requirements, and other compliance obligations.

First 90-Day Expectations

Days 1–30

Complete an initial operating assessment.
Establish KPI baseline and dashboard.
Map the sales-to-production-to-closeout workflow.
Identify recurring Owner operational interventions.
Clarify decision rights and escalation paths.
Begin the weekly leadership cadence.

Days 31–60

Implement a production-ready handoff checklist.
Publish leader scorecards.
Establish schedule and capacity reviews.
Assign accountable owners for recurring bottlenecks.
Present a written operating-improvement plan with priorities, owners, dates, and expected outcomes.

Days 61–90

Demonstrate an owner-light operating rhythm.
Provide reliable weekly executive reporting.
Show measurable improvement or a documented recovery plan for critical bottlenecks.
Lead the first formal leader scorecard reviews.
Present the next 90-day operating priorities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Senior operations leader with General Contractor construction operations experience.
Proven ability to lead production, project delivery, field teams, project managers, subcontractors, and cross-functional operating cadence.
Strong understanding of subcontractors, invoicing/billing readiness, permits/inspections, scheduling, capacity planning, vendor/material coordination, job-cost control, margin protection, quality, safety, customer escalation, and closeout.
Comfortable building dashboards, scorecards, SOPs, leadership meeting rhythms, and accountability systems.
Able to work closely with an Owner/CEO while independently owning routine operational decisions.
Direct, accountable, values-driven leader who can address hard issues respectfully and promptly.

Key Performance Areas

Revenue produced versus plan and backlog health.
Gross profit, job-cost variance, and margin leakage correction.
Job cycle time, production-ready backlog, schedule stability, and on-time completion.
Billing readiness, WIP coordination, and collections-risk reduction from operational delays.
Customer satisfaction, complaint resolution, review trends, warranty callbacks, and quality performance.
Safety incidents, near misses, training completion, permit/licensing/compliance exceptions, and corrective-action closure.
Leadership scorecard attainment, retention, manager development, and performance review completion.
CRM/project-system data accuracy, SOP adoption, dashboard quality, and continuous improvement.
